'''Sankar Das Sarma''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|æ|ŋ|k|ɑr|_|d|æ|ʃ|_|ˈ|ʃ|ɑr|m|ə}}) is an [[India]]-born American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical]] [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] [[physicist]]. He has been a member of the department of physics at [[University of Maryland, College Park]] since 1980.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.icts.res.in/people/sankar-das|title=Sankar Das Sarma|website=International Centre for Theoretical Sciences|access-date=2018-08-30}}</ref>

Das Sarma is the Richard E. Prange Chair in Physics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/people/faculty/current/item/114-dassarma.html|title=Das Sarma, Sankar|website=Department of Physics [[University of Maryland]]|access-date=2018-08-30}}</ref>  a distinguished university professor,<ref name=":0" /> a Fellow of the Joint Quantum Institute (JQI), and the director of the [[Condensed Matter Theory Center]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.umd.edu/cmtc/|title=Condensed Matter Theory Center webpage|website=Department of Physics University of Maryland|access-date=2018-08-30}}</ref> at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]]. 
As of 2025, he has mentored nearly 200 young physicists, including about 40 Ph.D. students and 150 postdoctoral researchers, more than 100 of whom have since become faculty members at universities around the world.<ref>{{cite web |title=Condensed Matter Theory Center – Introduction |url=https://www.physics.umd.edu/cmtc/intro.html
 }}</ref>
As of 2025, Das Sarma has published over 750 papers, garnering more than 100,000 citations, mostly in collaboration with his PhD students and postdoctoral fellows.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://jqi.umd.edu/news/jqi-fellow-sankar-das-sarma-elected-national-academy-sciences |title=JQI Fellow Sankar Das Sarma Elected to the National Academy of Sciences |website=Joint Quantum Institute |date=2026-05-01}}</ref> He was named a [[Highly Cited Researchers|Highly Cited Researcher]] by [[Clarivate]] (formerly [[Thomson Reuters]]) in every annual listing from 2014 to 2022.<ref name=":hcr2022">{{Cite web |title=Sankar Das Sarma Named Highly Cited Researcher |url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/about-us/news/department-news/1843-das-sarma-2022.html |website=Department of Physics, University of Maryland |date=November 16, 2022 |access-date=August 9, 2026}}</ref>

Das Sarma is a Fellow (in the Division of Condensed Matter Physics) of the [[American Physical Society]], and is a member (in the Physics section, with a secondary affiliation in the Applied Physics section) of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nasonline.org/news/2026-nas-election/ |title=2026 NAS Election |website=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

==Career==
Das Sarma came to the United States from India as a physics graduate student in 1974 after finishing his secondary school (Hare School in [[Kolkata]]) and undergraduate education at Presidency College in Calcutta, India (now Presidency University in Kolkata) where he was born. He received his PhD in theoretical physics from [[Brown University]] in 1979 as a doctoral student of [[John Quinn (physicist)|John Quinn]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/about-us/news/department-news/1226-das-sarma-receives-third-consecutive-honor-as-influential-researcher.html|title=Das Sarma Receives Third Consecutive Honor as Influential Researcher|date=18 November 2016|website=University of Maryland}}</ref>

In collaboration with [[Chetan Nayak]] and [[Michael Freedman]] of [[Microsoft Research]], Das Sarma introduced the <math>\nu=5/2 </math> [[Topological quantum computer|topological qubit]]  in 2005,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Das Sarma|first1=Sankar|last2=Freedman|first2=Michael|last3=Nayak|first3=Chetan|year=2005<!-- Deny Citation bot --> |title=Topologically Protected Qubits from a Possible Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall State|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=94|issue=16|article-number=166802|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.166802|pmid=15904258|bibcode=2005PhRvL..94p6802D|arxiv=cond-mat/0412343|s2cid=8773427}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=0707.1889|title=Topological Quantum Computation review article in Reviews of Modern Physics, 2008  |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics  |volume=80  |issue=3  |page=1083  |last1=Nayak  |first1=Chetan  |last2= Simon  |first2=Steven H.  |last3=Stern  |first3=Ady  |last4=Freedman  |first4=Michael  |author5=Sankar Das Sarma  |year=2007  |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.80.1083  |bibcode=2008RvMP...80.1083N  |s2cid=119628297 }}</ref> which has led to experiments in building a [[topological quantum computer|fault-tolerant quantum computer]] based on [[two-dimensional semiconductor]] structures.  Das Sarma's work on [[graphene]] has led to the theoretical understanding of graphene carrier transport properties at low densities where the inhomogeneous electron-hole puddles dominate the graphene landscape.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Adam|first1=Shaffique|last2=Hwang|first2=E. H.|last3=Galitski|first3=V. M.|last4=Sarma|first4=S. Das|date=2007-11-20|title=A self-consistent theory for graphene transport|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=104|issue=47|pages=18392–18397|doi=10.1073/pnas.0704772104|issn=0027-8424|pmc=2141788|pmid=18003926|bibcode=2007PNAS..10418392A|doi-access=free}}</ref>  In 2006 Das Sarma with Euyheon Hwang provided the basic theory for collective modes and dielectric response in graphene and related chiral two-dimensional materials.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Adam|first1=S.|last2=Hwang|first2=E.H.|last3=Rossi|first3=E.|last4=Das Sarma|first4=S.|date=2009|title=Theory of charged impurity scattering in two-dimensional graphene|journal=Solid State Communications|volume=149|issue=27–28|pages=1072–1079|doi=10.1016/j.ssc.2009.02.041|issn=0038-1098|arxiv=0812.1795|bibcode=2009SSCom.149.1072A|s2cid=330571}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Das Sarma|first1=S.|last2=Adam|first2=Shaffique|last3=Hwang|first3=E. H.|last4=Rossi|first4=Enrico|date=2011|title=Electronic transport in two-dimensional graphene|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=83|issue=2|pages=407–470|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.83.407|arxiv=1003.4731|bibcode=2011RvMP...83..407D|s2cid=118565433}}</ref> In 2011 Das Sarma and collaborators introduced a new class of lattice [[Tight binding|tight-binding]] flat-band systems with nontrivial [[Chern class|Chern numbers]] which belongs to the [[universality class]] of continuum [[Quantum Hall effect|quantum Hall]] and [[Fractional quantum Hall effect|fractional quantum Hall]] systems without any external magnetic fields.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sun|first1=Kai|last2=Gu|first2=Zhengcheng|last3=Katsura|first3=Hosho|last4=Das Sarma|first4=S.|date=2011-06-06|title=Nearly Flatbands with Nontrivial Topology|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.236803|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=106|issue=23|article-number=236803|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.236803|pmid=21770533|arxiv=1012.5864|s2cid=22738426}}</ref>  Such flat-band tight-binding systems with non-trivial Chern numbers have substantially enhanced the types of possible physical systems for the realization of topological matter.

In 2010, Das Sarma and collaborators, made a prediction that [[Majorana fermion]]s will be found in condensed matter,<ref>{{Cite journal  | last1=Lutchyn  | first1=Roman M.  | last2=Sau  | first2=Jay D.  | last3=Das Sarma  | first3=S.  | title=Majorana Fermions and a Topological Phase Transition in Semiconductor-Superconductor Heterostructures  | journal=Physical Review Letters  | volume=105  | issue=7  | article-number=077001  | year=2010  | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.105.077001  | url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.105.077001
| arxiv=1002.4033  }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/microsoft-advances-quantum-computing-how-did-do-mark-braunstein-aa2de/ |title=Microsoft Advances Quantum Computing: How Did They Do It? |author=Mark Braunstein |website=LinkedIn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Lewton|first=Thomas|title=The Near-Magical Mystery of Quasiparticles|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/like-magic-physicists-conjure-curious-quasiparticles-20210324/|access-date=2021-04-08|website=Quanta Magazine|language=en}}</ref> in particular, in semiconductor nanowires.<ref>{{Cite journal  | last1=Sau  | first1=Jay D.  | last2=Lutchyn  | first2=Roman M.  | last3=Tewari  | first3=Sumanta  | last4=Das Sarma  | first4=S.  | title=Generic New Platform for Topological Quantum Computation Using Semiconductor Heterostructures  | journal=Physical Review Letters  | volume=104  | issue=4  | article-number=040502  | year=2010  | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.040502  | url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.040502
| arxiv=0907.2239  }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal  | last1=Sau  | first1=Jay D.  | last2=Tewari  | first2=Sumanta  | last3=Lutchyn  | first3=Roman M.  | last4=Stanescu  | first4=Tudor D.  | last5=Das Sarma  | first5=S.  | title=Non-Abelian quantum order in spin-orbit-coupled semiconductors: Search for topological Majorana particles in solid-state systems  | journal=Physical Review B  | volume=82  | issue=21  | article-number=214509  | year=2010  | doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.82.214509  | url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.82.214509
| arxiv=1006.2829  }}</ref> 
This has led to considerable experimental activity, led by Microsoft Corporation, to produce a topological quantum computer.<ref>{{Cite journal  | last=Microsoft Quantum  | title=InAs-Al hybrid devices passing the topological gap protocol  | journal=Physical Review B  | volume=107  | issue=24  | article-number=245423  | year=2023  | doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.107.245423  | url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.107.245423| arxiv=2207.02472  }}</ref>

Among Das Sarma's many other notable contributions are the theory for nonequilibrium MBE growth (often referred to as the Das Sarma-Lai-Villain equation),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lai |first1=Z.-W.|last2=Das Sarma |first2=S. |date=1991-05-20 |title=Kinetic growth with surface relaxation: Continuum versus atomistic models |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=66 |issue=20 |pages=2348–2351 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.66.2348 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.66.2348}}</ref> theories for quantum localization in incommensurate one-dimensional lattice systems manifesting mobility edges,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Das Sarma |first1=S. |last2=He |first2=Song |last3=Xie |first3=X. C. |date=1988-10-31 |title=Mobility Edge in a Model One-Dimensional Potential |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=61 |issue=18 |pages=2144–2147 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2144 |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2144|url-access=subscription }}</ref> developing the theory of ferromagnetism in diluted magnetically doped semiconductors via magnetic polaron formation and generalized percolation,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kaminski |first1=A. |last2=Das Sarma |first2=S. |date=2002-05-31 |title=Polaron Percolation in Diluted Magnetic Semiconductors |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=88 |issue=24 |article-number=247202 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.88.247202 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.88.247202|arxiv=cond-mat/0201229 }}</ref> calculating the appropriate fractional quantum Hall gap energies as in the Zhang-Das Sarma model,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zhang |first1=F. C. |last2=Das Sarma |first2=S. |date=1986-02-15 |title=Excitation gap in the fractional quantum Hall effect: Finite layer thickness corrections |journal=Physical Review B |volume=33 |issue=4 |pages=2903–2905 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.33.2903 |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.33.2903|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and studies on the electronic structure of semiconductor heterostructures.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stern|first1=Frank |last2=Das Sarma |first2=S.|date=1984-07-15 |title=Electron energy levels in GaAs-Ga<sub>1−𝑥</sub>⁢Al<sub>𝑥</sub>⁢As heterojunctions |journal=Physical Review B |volume=30 |issue=2 |pages=840–849 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.30.840 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.30.840}}</ref>
Das Sarma has also made contributions to the understanding of many-body collective phenomena and quasiparticle renormalization effects in electron systems, work that helped establish the theoretical framework for electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions in low-dimensional systems.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://jqi.umd.edu/news/jqi-fellow-sankar-das-sarma-elected-national-academy-sciences |title=JQI Fellow Sankar Das Sarma Elected to the National Academy of Sciences |website=Joint Quantum Institute |date=2026-05-01}}</ref> This includes early theories of collective modes in two-dimensional semiconductors<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Das Sarma |first1=S. |last2=Madhukar |first2=A. |date=1981-01-15 |title=Collective modes of spatially separated, two-component, two-dimensional plasma in solids |journal=Physical Review B |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=805–815 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.23.805 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.23.805}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Das Sarma |first1=S. |last2=Quinn |first2=J. J. |date=1982-06-15 |title=Collective excitations in semiconductor superlattices |journal=Physical Review B |volume=25 |issue=12 |pages=7603–7618 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.25.7603 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.25.7603}}</ref> and coupled electron-phonon quasiparticle properties,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jalabert |first1=R. |last2=Das Sarma |first2=S. |date=1989-11-15 |title=Quasiparticle properties of a coupled two-dimensional electron-phonon system |journal=Physical Review B |volume=40 |issue=14 |pages=9723–9737 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.40.9723 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.40.9723}}</ref> as well as later work explaining why graphene behaves as a weakly interacting system despite its strong bare Coulomb coupling.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Das Sarma |first1=S. |last2=Hwang |first2=E. H. |last3=Tse |first3=Wang-Kong |date=2007-03-27 |title=Many-body interaction effects in doped and undoped graphene: Fermi liquid versus non-Fermi liquid |journal=Physical Review B |volume=75 |issue=12 |article-number=121406 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.75.121406 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.75.121406|arxiv=cond-mat/0610581 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Barnes |first1=Edwin |last2=Hwang |first2=E. H. |last3=Throckmorton |first3=R. E. |last4=Das Sarma |first4=S. |date=2014-06-25 |title=Effective field theory, three-loop perturbative expansion, and their experimental implications in graphene many-body effects |journal=Physical Review B |volume=89 |issue=23 |article-number=235431 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.89.235431 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.89.235431|arxiv=1401.7011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hofmann |first1=Johannes |last2=Barnes |first2=Edwin |last3=Das Sarma |first3=S. |date=2014-09-05 |title=Why Does Graphene Behave as a Weakly Interacting System? |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=113 |issue=10 |article-number=105502 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.113.105502 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.113.105502|arxiv=1405.7036 }}</ref>

Das Sarma is a coauthor on several comprehensive review articles on spintronics,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Žutić |first1=Igor |last2=Fabian |first2=Jaroslav |last3=Das Sarma |first3=S. |date=2004-04-23 |title=Spintronics: Fundamentals and applications |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=76 |issue=2 |pages=323–410 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.76.323 |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.76.323|arxiv=cond-mat/0405528 }}</ref> non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nayak |first1=Chetan |last2=Simon |first2=Steven H. |last3=Stern |first3=Ady |last4=Freedman |first4=Michael |last5=Das Sarma |first5=Sankar |date=2008-09-12 |title=Non-Abelian anyons and topological quantum computation |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=80 |issue=3 |pages=1083–1159 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.80.1083 |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.80.1083|arxiv=0707.1889 }}</ref> electronic transport in graphene,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Das Sarma |first1=S. |last2=Adam |first2=Shaffique |last3=Hwang |first3=E. H. |last4=Rossi |first4=Enrico |date=2011-05-16 |title=Electronic transport in two-dimensional graphene |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=83 |issue=2 |pages=407–470 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.83.407 |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.83.407|arxiv=1003.4731 }}</ref> and Majorana fermions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Das Sarma |first1=S. |last2=Freedman |first2=M. |last3=Nayak |first3=C. |date=2015-10-27 |title=Majorana zero modes and topological quantum computation |journal=npj Quantum Information |volume=1 |page=15001 |doi=10.1038/npjqi.2015.1 |arxiv=1501.02813 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Das Sarma |first1=S. |date=2023-02-06 |title=In search of Majorana |journal=Nature Physics |volume=19 |pages=165–170 |doi=10.1038/s41567-022-01900-9 |arxiv=2210.17365 }}</ref>
Das Sarma edited a well-known book on quantum Hall effects with comprehensive contributions from the leading quantum Hall researchers.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Das Sarma |first1=Sankar |last2=Pinczuk |first2=Aron |title=Perspectives in Quantum Hall Effects: Novel Quantum Liquids in Low-Dimensional Semiconductor Structures |publisher=Wiley |year=2008 |isbn=978-0-471-11216-7}}</ref>

He has been a visiting professor at many institutions during his professional career, including [[Technical University of Munich]], [[IBM]] [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center]], [[University of Hamburg]], [[Cambridge University]], [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], [[University of New South Wales]], [[Sandia National Laboratories]], [[University of Melbourne]], [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in Santa Barbara, Institute for Theoretical Physics in Beijing, and Microsoft Station Q Research Center.
<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.microsoft.com/stories/stationq/ |title=Microsoft Station Q |website=Microsoft News |publisher=Microsoft }}</ref>
